recovery-http.description: D-Link recovery mode (hold reset pin under device while powering on; works on both WAN and LAN ports). IMPORTANT: use recovery.bin (NOT factory.bin) for U-Boot recovery. ASU produces recovery.bin with custom settings baked in — works in single step. Stock recovery.bin also works but requires sysupgrade afterward for custom config. First NAND boot after U-Boot recovery flash takes 5+ minutes (stock) or ~80s (ASU with uci-defaults).
recovery-http.reset_instructions: Connect ethernet to any port (WAN or LAN). Use a pin to press and hold the reset button UNDER the device. Plug in power while holding reset. Hold for ~10-12 seconds until LED blinks red, then release.

dlink-hnap.description: D-Link stock firmware HNAP SOAP API firmware upload (no reset needed, works when router is running stock firmware)
dlink-hnap.notes: HNAP challenge-response auth with HMAC-MD5 + custom AES (HNAP_CONTENT). Login with default password, upload factory image via multipart POST. WARNING: GetFirmwareValidation rejects OpenWrt images on stock v1.02 (IsValid=false). Use recovery-http for reliable flashing.
dlink-hnap.caveat: Firmware upload API returns OK but stock firmware validation blocks non-D-Link images. The GPL RSA signing key is a test key, not the production key. Recovery-http (U-Boot) bypasses all validation.

reboot.recovery_mac_last_packet: TCP FIN after HTTP response body

sticker_credentials.description: Factory WiFi SSID/password and MAC addresses stored in NAND config2 partition

known_keys.factory_mac: LAN MAC address printed on device sticker

sticker_credentials.ssid_format: dlink-XXXX where XXXX is last 4 hex chars of MAC or random

recovery-http.notes: Stock recovery.bin from downloads.openwrt.org works reliably. ASU custom recovery.bin with USB use cases (tether-android-adb) causes boot failure — device has no USB port. Device falls back to U-Boot recovery after failed flash (not bricked). Post-flash SSH configuration is the recommended path: flash stock, then configure via SSH. Stock recovery.bin boots in ~90s. Port labeled 'ethernet' = LAN, 'internet' = WAN. Use LAN port for initial setup.

dlink-hnap.notes: Auth + upload works (returns OK). GetFirmwareValidation returns IsValid=false for OpenWrt images — stock firmware validation blocks non-D-Link firmware. Recovery-http is the proven method.

sysupgrade.notes: sysupgrade from stock OpenWrt 24.10.5 to ASU custom 24.10.2 build. Works via conwrt --request-image --wan-ssh. ~2m15s total. SSH key, random password, and WAN SSH all applied via ASU first-boot uci-defaults script.

recovery-http-25.12.5.notes: Full unattended recovery-http flash from U-Boot recovery mode to ASU custom 25.12.5 build (vpn-nordvpn static config, WiFi STA uplink, mgmt WiFi, keys, kill switch) on ai-legion-small/Ubuntu (direct cable). Upload ~41s, flash ~60s, boot ~90s. Verified end-to-end: SSH key auth, wg handshake, LAN NAT through tunnel to NordVPN DE exit (Hamburg). Note: host must reach 192.168.0.1 (recovery) and 192.168.1.1 (post-flash) — conwrt now manages both client aliases automatically.

vpn-nordvpn-wireguard.notes: vpn-nordvpn use case with config_file (dashboard-exported WireGuard conf). 5GHz STA uplink (wwan), wg0 full tunnel with netifd-managed endpoint route, lan→vpn forwarding, kill switch, NordVPN DNS via tunnel. Exit verified from LAN client: Hamburg, DE (PacketHub S.A.).

vpn-nordvpn-token-and-vpn-ap.notes: Token mode (build-time resolution via credentials + recommendations API) with 2.4GHz VPN-exit AP (SSID nord/nordnord). From-scratch sysupgrade first boot verified: br-vpnlan bridge, vpnap zone with vpnap→vpn forwarding, DHCP/DNS/management input rules, 20dBm radio, dnsmasq re-arm. Phone client associated (-44dBm) and received DHCP lease 172.16.31.238; wired client exit via NordVPN DE; kill switch blocks on ifdown wg0. E2E stories: tests/e2e/test_nordvpn_e2e.py (5 host-side pass; phone stories pending phone replug).

wifi_sta_ap.notes: Post-flash WiFi config verified: radio0=2g, radio1=5g. STA only, AP only, STA+AP all verified on real hardware.

vpn-nordvpn-openvpn.notes: vpn-nordvpn-openvpn use case: token-driven service credentials + DE server resolved at build time; template-faithful OpenVPN (multi-port 1231-1234, tls-auth, CN pin). Exit verified (UK box via API recommendation). Perf: 134-168 Mbps, 65-78% CPU. Configure-mode verified on-device; ASU bake path shares the same ops.

vpn-nordvpn-ikev2.notes: IKEv2/IPsec IKE_SA established (strongSwan 6.0.3, EAP-MSCHAPv2 with token creds, AES-CBC-256/HMAC-SHA2-256/MODP-2048, vip 10.6.0.22). ESP CHILD_SA blocked: SAD install EINVAL while eip93 crypto driver loaded (kernel 6.12.94, OpenWrt 25.12; kmod-ipsec4 present). rmmod of eip93 with live refs wedged the kernel - power cycle required. See README 'NordVPN IKEv2/IPsec on MT7621' for the full recipe and cautions.

bench_observations.recovery_idle_timeout_seconds: 300-480 (measured 2026-09-27: server exits recovery ~5-8 min after entry; a flash attempt started late finds stock firmware instead)

led_language.red_constant: boot attempt failed / post-flash limbo — device will fall back to recovery on next power cycle

bench_observations.dual_image_boot: MediaTek dual-image bootloader: first boot after a recovery flash copies main->backup partition and reboots once more before OpenWrt comes up (expect two reboots)
bench_observations.ports: cable must be in the port labeled 'ethernet' (LAN) for booted OpenWrt; recovery mode answers on either port
bench_observations.upload_client_sensitivity: 2026-09-27/28 elimination matrix on an ER6P-routed seat: FOUR recovery uploads (24.10.8 curl, 24.10.5 curl, 24.10.5 webkit-framed, 23.05.5 curl at the older 13,631,488-byte layout) — every upload sha-verified locally, byte-exact Content-Length, 'Upgrade successfully!', 100% size write-out; every boot: zero DUT packets, constant-red limbo, recovery fallback on power cycle. Version, multipart framing, and image-size theories all eliminated. Unit-specific hardware suspected (recovery-mode NAND write corruption — no bad-block management in the U-Boot recovery writer — or bootloader-variant verification reject). Discriminator: serial console (labeled header, 3.3V 115200 8n1); conwrt serial-flash bypasses the recovery HTTP server entirely if NAND is healthy.
